title: Paris garden
html_source:
Shakespeare uses “Paris-garden” to refer to the famous bear-garden kept by Robert de Paris in the reign of Richard II (See for example: Henry VIII, Act 5, Scene 4).

It was situated close to the Globe Theatre, on the southern bank of the Thames.
